title: Six habits, and what each one buys
caption: None of these make code faster. They make it shorter to read and harder to get wrong, and the first one — hand back a new list instead of rearranging the caller's — is the only one that fixes a real bug rather than a style complaint.

cells.label: build, don't change
cells.note: sorted(names) returns a new list; names.sort() rearranges the caller's

cells.label: comprehension
cells.note: [t for t in times if t < 40] — keep some, change some, one line

cells.label: sorted(key=…)
cells.note: key says which part to order by; a tuple key breaks ties

cells.label: unpacking
cells.note: a, b = b, a swaps; for name, time in pairs names both parts

cells.label: enumerate / zip
cells.note: position with the value; two lists walked side by side

cells.label: return early
cells.note: answer the awkward cases first, then write the real work unindented
